description: One message each that states values for more than one subject. Trap: an accepted claim whose value belongs to another subject than its own. The facts label who holds which value in the message; expect lists the facts a correct extraction asserts for their own subject. Synthetic; the labels are read only when grading.

items.text: My sister moved to Denver last spring, but I still live in Boston.
Robin, my colleague, is allergic to peanuts; I'm only allergic to cats.
My partner works at the hospital downtown while I work from home for a design studio.
Our dog turns nine this month, and I turn forty in June.
My brother's birthday is on March 3; mine is on June 12.
Sam from next door drives a red van. I just bought a bicycle to get to work.
My mother prefers tea in the evening, but I always drink coffee in the morning.
Robin speaks Portuguese at home; I only speak English and a little French.
The kids' school starts at 8:15, and my own shift starts at 9:30.
My manager is based in Lisbon; I report to her from the Leeds office.
My daughter is vegetarian. I eat everything except shellfish.
Sam's flight lands at gate 12; mine lands at gate 30 an hour later.
My grandfather grew up in Porto, and I grew up in Manchester.
Robin's car is the blue one. Mine is the grey hatchback parked outside.
My sister and I both live in Leeds now.
I have two cats, and so does Robin.
